summary: A hook is a script Git runs at a set moment, such as right before a commit. A pre-commit hook that exits with a non-zero code stops the commit.
notes: The file name picks the moment: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push, and others. .git/hooks has samples ending in .sample.
git clone does not copy .git/hooks. Teams keep hooks in the repository and copy them in, or set git config core.hooksPath hooks.
git commit --no-verify skips the pre-commit hook. Use it only when you know why the hook failed.
pitfall: A hook without execute permission does not run. Git prints a hint that the hook was ignored, and the commit goes through. Run chmod +x on it.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with one commit. The folder hooks/ holds a pre-commit script that is not installed yet.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF

cat > hooks/pre-commit <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Stop the commit if a staged line adds the word TODO.
# --no-color keeps color codes out of the text that grep reads.
if git diff --cached --no-color -U0 | grep -q '^+.*TODO'; then
  echo "pre-commit: remove TODO before you commit"
  exit 1
fi
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Start gradebook with hooks"
